judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate integration/enumeration language, but it ends with an order-of-precedence rule ('If anything in the other Contract Documents is inconsistent with this Agreement, this Agreement shall govern') whose reach over addenda and exhibits is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That precedence rule sits against Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 (inconsistencies resolved by better quality/more stringent requirement per the Architect) and A201 1.2.1 (documents complementary), so a court could have to reconcile competing conflict rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and standard: contractor fully executes the Work except as indicated to be others' responsibility; the exception is generic but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum replaces this with Article 2 [Revised], so the operative text is elsewhere; no substantive conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Approximately the Fifteenth of July' is inherently imprecise for a commencement date that drives the Contract Time.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.1 [Revised] fixes July 15, 2002 'pending approval of permits', which both supersedes and qualifies this clause and interacts with A201 8.1.2's definition of the date of commencement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One definite sentence measuring Contract Time from the date of commencement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 8.1.1-8.1.2 and Addendum 4.1; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The completion deadline is stated in a partly blank/garbled fill-in ('five hundred ___ calendar days'), leaving the intended period uncertain on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 4.3 [Revised] substitutes a fixed date of November 30, 2003, which does not obviously match any day count here, creating a potential inconsistency between the two completion terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Contract Sum as Cost of the Work plus Fee; the terms are defined elsewhere and the sentence itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge of a cost-plus contract whose Guaranteed Maximum Price is filled in as 'N/A' (5.2.1) while Articles 8, 12 and 13 assume a GMP exists, so its operation as a whole is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Fee is stated in words and figures that appear not to match ('Three Hundred ... Thousand Dollars ($380,000)'), the classic mechanical defect, and it is unclear whether the fee is a lump sum or a rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraphs 12.1.7.3, 13.2.2 and 6.4 all speak of 'the rate stated in Subparagraph 5.1.2' or of equitable fee adjustment, which fits awkwardly with a single fixed sum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guaranteed maximum figure is entered as 'N/A', so the clause purports to guarantee a maximum while stating none, and it then makes the Contractor bear costs exceeding that non-existent number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dozens of provisions (8.1.8, 10.2, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7.1-.2, 12.2.5, 13.2, 13.4) are built on a Guaranteed Maximum Price that this clause never supplies, a whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank fill-in for alternates with only the AIA instructional note; nothing substantive to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Refers to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves as 'N/A', but the blank makes the point academic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unit prices, if any, are as follows:' with nothing following; the clause is empty rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.3.9 and 7.3.3.2 contemplate unit prices 'stated in the Contract Documents'; the blank simply means they are not stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blank allowance fill-in; no operative words capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.8 governs allowances if any exist; the blank leaves nothing inconsistent, though Exhibits could be read as allowances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blank fill-in for assumptions underlying the GMP; nothing stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tied to the 'N/A' GMP in 5.2.1, but on its own adds nothing to the conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably inferable', 'further development' and 'changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality' are elastic boundary terms that decide whether work is extra.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates further design development to a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank, and Addendum 6.5's fast-track Change Order procedure covers similar ground differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to the methods listed in A201 7.3.3; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adjusts a GMP that does not exist under 5.2.1, and Addendum 6.5 supplies a different pricing/Change Order mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense but precise definitional cross-referencing of 'cost' and 'fee' in A201 clauses; a reader must track references but the meaning is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly disclaims modification by Articles 5, 7 and 8, which must be squared with 6.3's opposite instruction for GMP adjustments; the interplay is intricate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'fee' by reference to 'the Contractor's Fee as defined in Subparagraph 5.1.1', but the Fee is stated in 5.1.2 — a mis-citation that changes what the sentence points to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also sits directly against 6.2, which says the same A201 terms shall NOT be modified by Articles 5, 7 and 8 for subcontract adjustments; the two rules must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial inequity' and 'equitably adjusted' are open-textured standards that a court would have to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes fee-adjustment provisions 'in Paragraph 5.1' which the executed form does not contain, and it adjusts a GMP left as 'N/A'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs necessarily incurred in the proper performance of the Work' and 'rates not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project' are exactly the sort of standards parties fight over in a cost-plus job.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Cost of the Work 'shall include only the items set forth in this Article 7', yet Exhibits C and D add a 5% hand-tool markup, a 1% insurance charge and excise tax as job costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursable wages of workers directly employed at the site or, with approval, off site; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B fixes labor rates and Exhibit C adds 5% of payroll for hand tools, so what 'wages' means for billing is affected by the exhibits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Supervisory and administrative personnel when stationed at the site with the Owner's approval' leaves the approval and stationing tests to be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 [Revision] says the Fee covers senior management, executives and administrative support with none of it reimbursable under Article 7, which pulls against this reimbursement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only for that portion of their time required for the Work' is a workable, if fact-bound, limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Again in tension with Addendum 8.1.8 [Revision], which sweeps management and purchasing costs into the Fee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customary benefits such as sick leave, medical and health benefits, holidays, vacations and pensions' is an illustrative list whose outer edge is not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D prescribes a flat 1% insurance charge on labor and subcontract costs, which overlaps this insurance-cost category.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain reimbursement of the cost of materials incorporated in the Work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1.7.2 and A201 9.3.2 on stored materials; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable waste and spoilage' is a soft limit, though the ownership and credit mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article 9's credit-to-Owner scheme; no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Not customarily owned by construction workers' and 'fully consumed' are the contested boundary terms for tool charges, and 'cost less salvage value' adds another judgment call.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C says hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor' yet adds a flat 5% of payroll to cover the same tools, which cannot be squared easily with this reimbursement rule or with 8.1.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rental of equipment 'whether rented from the Contractor or others' with rates subject to Owner approval; the self-rental permission is clear if unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's Equipment Rate Sheet and Exhibit C's statement that rates are 'based upon standard rates paid at the place of the Project' overlay this, and 8.1.5 excludes rental costs except as provided here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite cost item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.15 clean-up obligations; nothing inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable petty cash expenses of the site office' is loose but small-bore.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 [Revision] assigns telephone, postage, supplies, facsimiles and stationery to the Fee, so the reimbursable/fee line for these items is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the reasonable expenses ... incurred while travelling in discharge of duties connected with the Work' invites argument about which travel qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 [Revision] puts 'all corporate vehicle charges' into the Fee, cutting across this allowance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires advance Owner approval and a mutually acceptable location; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 12.1.7.2 and A201 9.3.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract' is an allocation standard with no stated method.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D fixes the general liability premium at a flat 1% of labor and subcontract costs, which is a different measure from 'directly attributed' premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sales, use or similar taxes related to the Work; a recognised category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D's general excise tax computation (on all direct costs except subcontract costs, with an expanded definition of 'Subcontract' costs) supplies a specific and arguably inconsistent method.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permit and inspection fees the Contractor is required by the Contract Documents to pay; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.7.1 and 2.2.2 (Owner pays easements/assessments); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exception-laden but cross-referenced test for laboratory fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties to A201 13.5.3 and 7.7.3; the references are coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully structured; the carve-out that legal costs are 'not subject to the Guaranteed Maximum Price' is the only soft spot.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out presupposes a GMP that 5.2.1 leaves as 'N/A', and it interlocks with A201 3.17.1 on royalties and infringement defence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Data processing costs related to the Work' is broad but short; 'related to' is the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 [Revision] assigns all accounting services and main-office expense to the Fee, which overlaps data processing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposits lost other than through the Contractor's negligence; a clear allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.1.6's negligence exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes costs 'arising from disputes between the Owner and Contractor' and conditions the rest on prior written approval not unreasonably withheld; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 4.5/4.6 dispute machinery; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ties reimbursement to the 'Contractor's standard personnel policy', an extrinsic and unfixed document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Requires Owner approval, consistent with 7.7.1; no internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A catch-all for 'other costs' gated by advance written approval; the gate is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with 8.1.7 (no cost outside Article 7) and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 (changes only by Change Order, no course of dealing), which restrict informal approvals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Emergency costs by reference to A201 10.6; definite in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum's 7.7.2 [Revision] restates this with two new exclusions, so the same number carries two texts and the narrower one should control.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility' and insurance-recoverability are fact-bound but standard tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 7.7.3 [Revision] adds a further proviso about the Contractor's failure to maintain insurance, superseding this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in line to the exclusion list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces Article 8, which is repeatedly cross-referenced; nothing inconsistent on its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes principal-office salaries 'except as specifically provided in 7.2.2 and 7.2.3 or as may be provided in Article 14', an open-ended exception to a specific exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 14 of the Agreement contains no such personnel provision, and Addendum 14.6 [New] replaces 14.6 with warranties, so the referenced exception has no home.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Expenses of the Contractor's principal office and offices other than the site office' is short and categorical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.5.4 allows certain communication and site-office expenses and Addendum 8.1.8 elaborates the same divide, so the boundary is worked out across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overhead and general expenses, except as may be expressly included in Article 7' is a general exclusion measured against enumerated specifics — the classic general-versus-specific tension in a cost-plus contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7 items such as 7.5.4, 7.6.6 and Exhibit C's 5% payroll adder look like overhead, so the exclusion and the enumeration pull apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes rental costs of machinery except as provided in 7.5.2; definite cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's Equipment Rate Sheet bills Contractor-owned equipment at fixed rates, which must be squared with this exclusion and with 7.5.2's approval requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Negligence-based exclusion carved back by 7.7.3; the wording is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with 7.7.3 and its Addendum revision; no separate inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' is an expressio unius sweep whose interaction with the enumerated list is the whole question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits C and D add charges (5% hand-tool adder, 1% insurance rate, excise tax) that are not 'specifically and expressly described in Article 7', so this exclusion and the exhibits collide.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It bars costs that would cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded, but no such price is stated in 5.2.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum uses the same number 8.1.8 for a wholly different provision (Fee covers overhead), so the instrument contains two competing 8.1.8s in addition to the missing GMP.
